title: Duel Citizenship
cn: 第 5 集 · 双重国籍
novel:
Robin had lived in America for years, but her Canadian [[roots|root]] ran deep. When her work [[visa|visa]] came up for renewal, she faced a choice: apply for American [[citizenship|citizenship]], or return home.

Marshall, [[proud|proud]] of his American [[heritage|heritage]], argued she should stay. A loud [[debate|debate]] followed. Barney, never one to miss a joke, [[invaded|invade]] a Canadian bar and [[declared|declare]] that Canada was America's hat.

Robin felt torn. She loved New York, but she [[missed|miss]] the snow of her childhood, the polite strangers, the sound of [[hockey|hockey]] on a frozen pond.

"I don't want to [[abandon|abandon]] who I am," she told Ted.

Ted [[understood|understand]]. "You don't have to choose. That's the [[compromise|compromise]]."

In the end, Robin kept her Canadian [[identity|identity]] while building an American life. Some [[loyalties|loyalty]], she learned, did not require a [[passport|passport]]. They lived in the heart, where [[borders|border]] meant nothing.

root.en: the origin or deep connection to a place

visa.en: an official mark allowing you to enter a country

citizenship.en: being a legal member of a country

proud.en: feeling pleased about something you have done

heritage.en: traditions passed down through a culture

debate.en: a discussion in which people argue for different sides

invade.en: to enter a place in large numbers, often by force

miss.en: to feel sad because someone is not with you

hockey.en: a game played on ice with sticks and a puck

abandon.en: to leave someone or something completely

compromise.en: an agreement where each side gives up something

loyalty.en: staying true to someone or something

passport.en: a book that lets you travel between countries

border.en: the line that separates two countries
